parts.text:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Higher serum vitamin D was associated with lower odds of depression after adjusting for confounders.
Sentence: "A significant relationship between serum vitamin D with depression after adjusting for potential confounders was observed as well (OR 0.93, CI 0.87-0.99)."
Measured as: depression (major depressive disorder diagnosed by DSM criteria)
Population: Depressed (MDD diagnosed by psychiatrists) and matched healthy subjects; serum vitamin D measured in a randomly selected subset
Intervention: Serum vitamin D concentration (observational exposure)
Comparator: Healthy matched controls
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 330
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D supplementation at baseline was not associated with depression at 2.5 years in people with multiple sclerosis.
Sentence: "Vitamin D supplementation and meditation were not associated with outcomes."
Measured as: depression
Population: People with multiple sclerosis from the HOLISM study who completed baseline and 2.5-year follow-up surveys
Intervention: Vitamin D supplementation (self-reported, assessed at baseline)
Comparator: No vitamin D supplementation
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 1,401
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

{
  "rationale": "The studies differ in population (general MDD patients and healthy controls vs people with multiple sclerosis), exposure (measured serum vitamin D vs self-reported baseline supplementation), and study design (case-control vs prospective cohort).",
